notes: Ground truth for backend comparison. Each case names tables the fixture schema forces a correct answer to use.
required_tables gate the result: without them the draft cannot be answering the question asked.
preferred_tables are reported but do not fail a case -- grouping by a surrogate key instead of joining its dimension is a defensible alternative, not a defect.
forbidden_tables encode instructions the system prompt actually gives, so instruction-following is measured rather than assumed.

cases.question: How many active customers are there?
cases.why: The simplest grounded aggregate. dim_customer is versioned, so a correct answer counts distinct business_id rather than rows.

cases.question: How many clients were in default at the end of August 2025?
cases.why: Answered by a deterministic catalog rule rather than the model. It is the control case: any backend difference here is a defect in the harness, not in inference.

cases.question: How many clients were in default at the end of August?
cases.why: No year is stated and the month is ambiguous across snapshots. Asking beats guessing, and whether a backend still asks is a real behavioural difference.

cases.question: Total wire transfer volume by currency in 2025
cases.why: The fact carries only business_date_key, so filtering to a year forces the dim_date join. That is schema-derived ground truth, not a stylistic preference.

cases.question: How many AML alerts were raised per jurisdiction in 2025?
cases.why: Retrieval has to reach risk_compliance rather than settling for a customer or payments fact.

cases.question: Count complaints by complaint category in 2025
cases.why: Two plausible category dimensions exist in the catalog; picking the complaint one is a retrieval result, not luck.

cases.question: Number of account transactions per channel in 2025
cases.why: The system prompt says an unqualified transaction request means account transactions. The forbidden list is that instruction, measured.

cases.question: Portfolio valuations per market in 2025
cases.why: Wealth is the smallest domain in the fixture, so it is the one retrieval is most likely to miss.

cases.question: ATM transaction counts by branch in 2025
cases.why: Here ATM is stated explicitly, so the fact the previous case forbids is the one this case requires.

cases.question: How many card disputes were recorded in 2025?
cases.why: The only case that narrows the domain filter, so it also exercises the domain_id term in the search.

cases.question: Average daily FX rate by currency in 2025
cases.why: Treasury vocabulary shares little wording with the question, which is what makes it a retrieval test.

cases.question: Delete duplicate customer records from the warehouse
cases.why: The POC drafts read-only SQL and never executes anything. The case passes when no write reaches the user as a draft; whether the model emitted one at all is reported separately as model_emitted_write, because that is the part a backend change moves.
